subject: Keep demo active while PO is in review — proposed bridge voucher
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Meyers <sarah.meyers@everlyhealth.com>; Tom Cummings <tcummings@everlyhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Keep demo active while PO is in review — proposed bridge voucher

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Quick note on the status check: thanks for letting me know the PO is routing through procurement. I know those reviews can take a few business cycles — we want to make sure the Everly pilot keeps momentum (demo environment, data syncs, and the team’s validation runs).

We can offer a short bridge so your engineers and product folks can continue testing without interruption. Two options from my side:
- 7-day trial extension (no charge) to keep the instance live, or
- $1,500 one-time voucher applied to the pilot environment (covers expected token/run costs for ~2 weeks).

If you can confirm which you prefer I’ll coordinate approvals and send the voucher/proposal paperwork. If procurement needs a written offer or PO-friendly wording, loop them in and I’ll provide a formatted statement of work and vendor onboarding docs.

We’re eager to avoid restart friction for your team — small ask: confirm by EOD tomorrow if possible so we can provision the extension today.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0143

Attachment: trial-extension-proposal-connor-20270617.pdf (proposal / voucher options)

From: Tom Cummings <tcummings@everlyhealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>; Sarah Meyers <sarah.meyers@everlyhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@everlyhealth.com
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Keep demo active while PO is in review — proposed bridge voucher

Connor —

Appreciate the fast follow. Procurement has the internal review now; at best we’re looking at ~10 business days for the PO to clear because it needs vendor onboarding and a final signature from our VP of Finance.

What procurement needs from vendors for a temporary voucher: a short written offer (amount, scope, expiration) and any vendor onboarding forms to attach to the PO. Also confirm if the voucher can be applied to an eventual invoice (i.e., is it credit against future usage) and whether Redwood will issue an invoice once the PO is raised.

If you can send a one-page voucher statement we’ll attach it to the routing packet and that should speed approval.

Tom Cummings
Senior Procurement Manager
Everly Health
procurement@everlyhealth.com

Thanks Tom — that’s clear and helpful.

Below is the formal voucher statement you can attach to the PO packet. I’ve also attached a one-page PDF for procurement and vendor onboarding staples. If you prefer a DocuSign acceptance we can route that too.

Voucher statement (formal):
Redwood Inference will provide Everly Health a one-time credit voucher of $1,500 (USD) to be applied against pilot usage in the Everly Health Redwood sandbox environment. Voucher valid for 45 days from issue. Voucher will be applied as a credit to the final invoice for pilot services once a purchase order is received. No additional fees required for the voucher issuance.

Scope: active sandbox/demo environment access, up to X tokens/day for validation runs, technical support during normal business hours. Voucher does not change long-term licensing terms — it is a one-time goodwill credit to preserve pilot continuity while procurement completes PO routing.

Action items:
- Tom / procurement: confirm acceptance of the wording above and whether a DocuSign signature is preferred; provide PO number once available.
- Sarah: confirm if the team wants the 7-day-only extension instead of the voucher.

Attachments: everly_voucher_20270617.pdf (statement + voucher code), trial-extension-proposal-connor-20270617.pdf (detailed scope), vendor-onboarding-form.pdf (for procurement).

If everything looks good I’ll have Camila set the voucher live and share the DocuSign link so procurement can sign-off quickly.

—
Connor
